name: Audio-gd
_terms_not_concluded: Measured 2026-11-25. No terms page found on audio-gd.com, so no prohibition could be checked - NOT the same as finding no prohibition. The English navigation has seven items and no legal link; terms.htm, legal.htm, Copyright.htm and Privacy.htm all 404; Warranty-EN.htm was read in full and is a repair-and-shipping policy with no clause on content; there is no robots.txt (404). Every page carries the same footer, quoted as printed: « Copyright(C) 2004 www.audio-gd.com All Rights Reserved » - a bare reservation stating no prohibition on quoting. Records were written because nothing forbidding was found, with the quality of the check recorded on each one.
_NOS_settled_site_wide: 109 pages searched for « New Old Stock » and « N.O.S. »: ZERO hits. And the maker defines the term outright: « In the 1970'S, the first generation of CDP were released , and they used an NOS design . "NOS" stands for "Non Oversampling". » The valve products are where the other meaning would have appeared - the Vacuum HE-1 MK3's pages contain no occurrence of NOS at all. So vocabulary/nos-means-two-things.json is settled for this brand in the direction the catalogue cares about. This is the single most valuable terminological finding of the harvest so far: Audio-gd is the largest source of non-oversampling devices in the base, and the one brand where the ambiguity would have been most expensive.
_the_site_is_four_files_per_product: For a product page X.htm there are siblings X_Specs.htm, X_Use.htm and X_Custom.htm, and THE SPEC TABLE AND THE INPUT LIST LIVE IN THE SIBLINGS. Anyone fetching only the page named in the index gets no specifications at all. Two filename traps measured: the R-1 NOS's spec page is R2R/R1NOS/R1EN_Specs.htm, not R1NOSEN_Specs.htm; and R2R/DI25/DI25EN.htm's own tab links point at DI25HE's spec pages, so DI-25's own file is reachable only by guessing its name. Recorded because a future pass over the ~25 remaining discontinued R-2R models will hit the same structure.
_the_published_numbers_are_the_OS8_numbe: Every spec table is headed « Specifications tested by OS8 mode » - the S/N and THD figures are measured with 8x oversampling running, not in the non-oversampling mode that makes these devices worth cataloguing. The maker is explicit about the cost: « if you want good specs, the NOS design definitely is not for you », and its own NOS-only models publish THD+N of <0.03% where the oversampling siblings publish <0.01%. So for this brand the measurements and the interesting state describe two different configurations of one device.
_mojibake_warning_for_any_importer: Every page's Chinese text decodes to mojibake: the files declare charset=big5 while carrying GB-encoded bytes. Stray characters appear INSIDE spec tables, between a row label and its value. Any automated row-splitter must drop them, and they are not part of any value.
_still_to_harvest: Discontinued.htm holds roughly 25 further R-2R and PCM1704 converters on the same four-file pattern - R-7, R-7 MK2, R-7HE, R-7HE MK2, R-8HE, R-8 MK2, R-11 MK2, R-121, R-2R 1, R2R-11, R2R-2, the R-28 2019 to 2022 series, R-821, R-27 21, DAC19, NFB-7 and the RE line - plus about 90 other withdrawn models that are not converters. The DI-20, DI-25 and DI-25HE were read and deliberately NOT recorded: they convert digital to digital, so they do not belong in a DAC catalogue. Their figures are worth noting as the upstream limit though - the DI-20's coaxial output carries 384 kHz, twice what any of this maker's own DACs accept on coaxial.
